links.measured_arm_schedule: For each benchmark case and replicate r=1..20: odd r runs go-baseline, go-baseline-aa, go-candidate; even r runs go-candidate, go-baseline-aa, go-baseline. The six cases are run in the listed order.

question: Can a Go coordinator implementation that avoids per-entry LogAt allocation and cgo crossings preserve exact version-vector and delta semantics while materially reducing allocations, wall time, and CPU time on fixed 1,024- and 8,192-entry logs?

claims.text: The candidate returns the same ordered delta lines and reached version vectors as the baseline and passes the existing coordinator correctness and race gates.
claims.if_supported: the candidate is semantically admissible for the measured performance comparison
claims.if_not_supported: the candidate is rejected regardless of performance

claims.text: On the caught-up 8,192-entry workload, the candidate materially reduces bytes and allocations per operation without regressing any registered benchmark case.
claims.if_supported: an engineering allocation improvement limited to the registered Go coordinator workloads

claims.text: On the caught-up 8,192-entry workload, the candidate materially reduces both wall and process CPU nanoseconds per operation beyond the A/A spread, without regressing any registered benchmark case.
claims.if_supported: an engineering speedup limited to the registered Go coordinator workloads and pinned host class
claims.if_not_supported: no wall-time or CPU-time speedup is claimed

randomization.arm_order_reason: A fixed mirrored sequence is used because there are exactly three arms: odd replicates run baseline/AA/candidate and even replicates reverse the endpoints; this balances monotonic drift while keeping the schedule auditable before data.

seed_derivation.note: 0x5eed is the only coordinator job seed; fixture generation is deterministic and identical for all arms and repetitions.

instance_sampling.rule: Exhaustively run the six benchmark cases listed in links.benchmark_cases; there is no post-freeze sampling or case selection.

blinding.how: Not masked: build provenance and binary identity must be checked before accepting each row.

power.note: Twenty paired repetitions target the preregistered large effects (at least 25% time reduction and 90% byte reduction), not small effects. Holm correction covers wall and CPU comparisons across six cases; allocation gates are counted and also reported with paired intervals.

preflight_runtime.measured_on: Conservative preregistered planning bound from six cases, 20 fixed repetitions, and a 20-minute process timeout; no timed benchmark was run.

primary.name: allocated bytes per operation
primary.definition: Total Go heap bytes allocated during the b.N operation loop divided by b.N; deterministic fixture construction and correctness hashing are excluded.

primary.name: allocations per operation
primary.definition: Go heap allocation events during the b.N operation loop divided by b.N; setup and post-timing correctness work are excluded.

secondary.name: wall nanoseconds per operation
secondary.definition: Go testing benchmark elapsed monotonic wall time around only the b.N operation loop, divided by b.N.

secondary.name: process CPU nanoseconds per operation
secondary.definition: Difference in process user plus system CPU time from getrusage around the b.N operation loop, divided by b.N; fixture and correctness hashing are excluded.
secondary.resolution: 10 ns/op at fixed b.N=100 from a 1 us getrusage counter

secondary.name: ordered delta-line digest
secondary.definition: SHA-256 over each returned line prefixed by its little-endian uint64 byte length, in returned order, computed after timing.

secondary.name: canonical version-vector digest
secondary.definition: SHA-256 over peer:sequence newline records sorted by peer, computed after timing for the returned or reached vector.
secondary.source: benchmark correctness vector_sha256 or reached_vector_sha256 log field

counters: getrusage RUSAGE_SELF user plus system CPU time

placement.numa_policy: CPU and memory on one NUMA node

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed design: 3 arms x 6 benchmark cases x (3 warmups + 20 measured repetitions) = 414 invocations, each at exactly 100 benchmark operations, then stop.
No result-dependent early stopping, extension, case removal, or additional repetition is permitted; infrastructure failures are retained and are not retried under this protocol.
Any digest, vector, line-count, log-length, unit-test, or race-test mismatch rejects the candidate and stops performance interpretation, while already collected rows remain archived.

invalidation_rules: Reject the candidate if any benchmark assertion fails or candidate correctness digest differs from its paired baseline digest.
Reject the candidate if go test ./... or the named coordinator tests fail; reject for release if go test -race ./... fails. Race-instrumented timing is never used as performance evidence.

A timing row below L2 isolation, with changed affinity, thermal throttling, nonzero steal, material PSI contention, binary/hash mismatch, Go/C compiler mismatch, or b.N other than 100 is invalid for wall and CPU comparisons; its exact correctness fields remain reportable.
A row with missing -benchmem fields is invalid for allocation comparisons.
Profiled or perf-instrumented diagnostic rows are excluded from the decisive unprofiled distributions.
No invalid row is replaced except by a separately frozen amendment filed before seeing affected candidate results.

decision_rule.text: First require C-correct and a valid A/A control: all paired exact digests must match, all correctness gates must pass, baseline/AA allocation medians must be within 2%, baseline/AA wall and CPU median ratios must each lie in [0.95,1.05], and their 95% paired intervals must include 1. C-allocation is supported only if, for DeltaSinceCaughtUp/log_8192, the candidate/baseline median B/op ratio is at most 0.10 and allocs/op ratio is at most 0.25, while no registered case exceeds 1.05 for either allocation metric. C-time is supported only if, for that same decisive case, candidate/baseline median wall and CPU ratios are each at most 0.75 and each Holm-corrected 95% paired interval lies wholly below 1, while no registered case has a wall or CPU median ratio above 1.05. Each claim is decided separately; failure of any gate yields no claim for that metric.
decision_rule.threshold: Correctness exact; A/A allocation within 2% and time within 5%; decisive caught-up-8192 B/op <=0.10x, allocs/op <=0.25x, wall <=0.75x, CPU <=0.75x; all-case regression ceiling 1.05x.
decision_rule.statistic: Within each benchmark case, pair arms by replicate and report candidate/baseline and baseline-AA/baseline median ratios for B/op, allocs/op, wall ns/op, and CPU ns/op.
decision_rule.interval: 95% paired bootstrap interval over the 20 fixed replicate pairs for each metric and benchmark case; exact digest and test gates have no interval.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: candidate/baseline median ratio and percent change, with the baseline/AA ratio as the empirical noise floor

graphs: paired candidate/baseline and baseline-AA/baseline ratios by benchmark case for B/op and allocs/op
paired candidate/baseline and baseline-AA/baseline ratios by benchmark case for wall and CPU ns/op
